name: Lard
label: Alternative Tentacles
lede: Jello Biafra showed up at Chicago Trax with newspaper clippings instead of lyrics, and [[Al Jourgensen]] and [[Paul Barker]] turned them into songs. Lard has never officially toured, and it keeps getting announced anyway.

eras.title: Clippings instead of lyrics
eras.text: Jello Biafra had been out of Dead Kennedys for two years when he landed in Chicago with the Ministry crew. The first Lard sessions started with a name, a stack of cuttings and a studio co-owner who would soon end up on a record sleeve.

years.src: Punknews: Jello Biafra Walks Us Through · Wikipedia: Lard (band)
yt: Lard: Ministry and Dead Kennedys unite
years.h: Biafra names the band Lard on the spot
years.p: Al Jourgensen had just asked what to call it. By Biafra's account, Jourgensen laughed so hard he ended up on the floor.
years.xp:
Biafra told Punknews that the name came straight out of his head, and that Jourgensen laughed so hard he ended up on the floor. Wikipedia dates the band's founding to 1988, when it started as a side project with Jourgensen, bassist [[Paul Barker|5bec856f-b78b-4216-8af5-1c0c6365bcbe]] and drummer [[Jeff Ward|90023d8a-3907-45ec-a2aa-b8da61a6d0bd]], all from the [[Ministry|13df2a46-f72f-40e7-aa63-26fcf62c7048]] orbit.

Biafra also said he had heard Ministry's records and knew he had to work with Jourgensen again, a hint that the two had crossed paths before Lard.

years.big: "One liners that I remembered or things that I cut out of the Chicago Tribune."
years.src: Punknews: Jello Biafra Walks Us Through · Wikipedia: The Power of Lard
years.h: Biafra brings newspaper cuttings to Chicago Trax instead of lyrics
years.p: That is how Biafra described the raw material for the first Lard EP, recorded in 1988 at the studio Ministry used.
years.xp:
Only afterwards did Biafra notice the songs shared a theme: controlling people through anxiety about how they look.

Wikipedia lists the recording at Chicago Trax Studios in 1988, with producer credits going to Hypo Luxa, Hermes Pan and Count Ringworm. Reid Hyams, who co-owned the studio and produced the first EP, would get his name into a Lard album title two years later.

years.cap: Sleeve of the 1989 Alternative Tentacles 12-inch of The Power of Lard
years.h: The Power of Lard ends on a 31-minute track
years.p: The Alternative Tentacles debut is three songs and 43 minutes, and "Time to Melt" alone runs 31:55. It reached number 4 on the UK Indie Chart.
years.xp:
The EP has the title track (7:29), "Hellfudge" (5:04) and "Time to Melt". Trouser Press called it "a casual and exciting bit of supergrouping"; Music Week's Jerry Smith found it "rather predictable."

The title track found a second audience in 1996, when it soundtracked a section of the skateboard video Toy Machine: Welcome to Hell, per Wikipedia.

eras.title: Reid on the back cover
eras.text: Lard's first live outings came as guests on Ministry's own shows. Then it made a full album in the same Chicago studio, with a drummer's chair that was starting to be shared.

years.src: Wikipedia: In Case You Didn't Feel Like Showing Up · Wikipedia: Lard (band)
yt: Ministry with Jello Biafra: The Power of Lard, Feb 22 1990
years.h: Partway through Ministry's set, Biafra walks on with a rewritten Pledge of Allegiance
years.p: After "Stigmata" on February 22 at the Holiday Star Theatre in Merrillville, Indiana, he delivered his version of the Pledge, then stayed for a Lard song.
years.xp:
The show became Ministry's live album In Case You Didn't Feel Like Showing Up, released September 4, 1990. Wikipedia notes the video mixes that night with a December 1989 New Year's Eve show in Chicago, and the band wore identical clothes on both dates so the edit would match.

Lard played during Ministry's 1988 tour and throughout its 1989 and 1990 dates, according to Wikipedia. "The Power of Lard" is credited to Jourgensen, Barker, Ward and Biafra on the 2017 reissue, running 8:11 live.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Last Temptation of Reid · Punknews: Jello Biafra Walks Us Through
years.h: Reid Hyams, the studio co-owner, gets his name on Lard's first album
years.p: The Last Temptation of Reid is named for the man who produced the EP at Chicago Trax, and his photo is on the back cover.
years.xp:
Recorded in May 1990 at Chicago Trax and released on Alternative Tentacles, it borrows its title from the Scorsese film with Reid swapped in. It includes a reworked "They're Coming to Take Me Away, Ha-Haaa!" with guitar added and an extra verse by Biafra. Vinyl runs 41:38, the CD and cassette 56:07, and Wikipedia says the album reached number 69 on the UK Albums Chart.

Biafra told Punknews the sessions could resemble "a Marx brothers movie," and that Reid was made to pose for the back cover.

eras.title: Ministry gets huge, Lard goes quiet
eras.text: Ministry's profile grew and Lard recorded little. Then the drummer who had been there from the first sessions died.

years.src: Wikipedia: Jeff Ward (musician) · Ministry Music: Jeff Ward Obituary
years.h: Drummer Jeff Ward dies at 30 in Chicago
years.p: Per Wikipedia, Ward died by suicide by carbon monoxide poisoning. He had played on the first Lard EP and album.
years.xp:
Ward had played with Ministry, Revolting Cocks and [[Nine Inch Nails|b7ffd2af-418f-4be2-bdd1-22f8b48613da]], and sang and drummed in Lard. A Ministry fan-site obituary citing the Chicago Sun-Times (May 6, 1993) says he died at his West Side home, that he had struggled with addiction, and quotes his brother Jason. A tribute concert was held at the Thirsty Whale in River Grove, Illinois, where Ward had played as a teenager.

Revolting Cocks' Linger Ficken' Good (1993) and Ministry's Filth Pig (1996) carry dedications to him, per Wikipedia.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Last Temptation of Reid
years.h: Natural Born Killers puts "Forkboy" in front of a bigger crowd
years.p: The opening track of The Last Temptation of Reid reached far more people through the film, and has since been covered by Flotsam and Jetsam and Black Light Burns.

eras.title: A record that took a decade
eras.text: Pure Chewing Satisfaction and 70's Rock Must Die came out of sessions spread across a decade, with Bill Rieflin behind the kit and some of Jeff Ward's earlier tracks folded in.

years.src: Wikipedia: Pure Chewing Satisfaction · Brainwashed: Pure Chewing Satisfaction review
yt: Lard: Pure Chewing Satisfaction, full album
years.h: Pure Chewing Satisfaction pulls in sessions from 1990 to 1997
years.p: The second Lard album draws on recordings from May 1990, 1991 to 1992 and 1995 to 1997 at Chicago Trax, and ships with a 30-page insert of absurd newspaper clippings.
years.xp:
Bill Rieflin drums on most tracks, with Ward and Rey Washam on some and Mike Scaccia guitar on several songs. The Fort Worth Star-Telegram called the sound "Ministry's 'Just One Fix' times eight"; NME gave it 8 out of 10.

Brainwashed's reviewer liked the packaging, a 30-page insert that recalls the collage style of [[Dead Kennedys|37c78aeb-d196-42b5-b991-6afb4fc9bc2e]] releases, and found some tracks repetitive.

years.src: Alternative Tentacles: Lard · Wikipedia: 70's Rock Must Die
years.h: 70's Rock Must Die, and a 1979 Ford Pinto for sale
years.p: The three-track EP ends with "Ballad of Marshall Ledbetter", inspired by a real protest in the Florida state capitol.
years.xp:
Alternative Tentacles says the release came with an auction of a vintage 1979 Ford Pinto with period-appropriate decor. The tracks are "70s Rock Must Die" (7:07), "Volcanus 2000 (We Wipe the World)" (6:14) and the Ledbetter song (5:06).

Wikipedia says it draws on the same sessions as the last album, and lists Metal Hammer's 8 out of 10.

eras.title: Announced, again
eras.text: Lard never officially toured. It turned up for a handful of Ministry shows, lost another drummer, and has been announced as coming back more than once.

years.h: Lard plays the end of Ministry's Los Angeles show
years.p: Biafra, Jourgensen and Barker played a Lard set to close Ministry's concert in Los Angeles.

years.h: Lard shows up on three Ministry dates in September 2004
years.p: San Francisco on the 26th, Portland on the 28th and Seattle on the 29th all included Lard appearances.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists these as the only other Lard shows besides the 1988 to 1990 Ministry tours and the 2003 Los Angeles date. As of 2007, Antiwarsongs described the band as having never launched an official tour.

years.src: Rolling Stone: Bill Rieflin · BNR Metal Pages: Lard
years.h: Bill Rieflin, drummer on the last two Lard records, dies at 59
years.p: Ministry called him "an integral part of Ministry's developments and success" after his death in March 2020.
years.xp: Rieflin played on Pure Chewing Satisfaction and 70's Rock Must Die, and later played with R.E.M. and King Crimson. Rolling Stone's report gives no cause of death.

years.big: "His brain is different than most brains, man."
years.src: Wikipedia: Lard (band) · Stereogum: We've Got A File On You · Jello Biafra's Renegade Roundtable
years.h: Jourgensen keeps saying a new Lard album is coming
years.p: Jourgensen on Biafra, to Stereogum in 2024. He has said the two would email songs back and forth to make a new record, per Wikipedia.
years.xp: Jourgensen also said he and Biafra still hook up in a studio whenever they are in the same town. The first episode of Biafra's Renegade Roundtable podcast, released October 21, 2022, was a conversation with Jourgensen that touches on Lard.

years.h: Paul Barker rejoins Al Jourgensen for a final Ministry album
years.p: The bassist who had been in Lard since the start came back to the Ministry fold in March 2024, per Wikipedia.
years.xp: Barker said in 2015 that he was "fairly confident we will not work together," but the two reconciled at documentary screenings in 2018, according to Wikipedia. Jourgensen has also suggested one final Lard album is possible, per AllMusic and Antiwarsongs.
